cards.interpretation: According to WHO 5th Edition 2022, KIT p.D816V with VAF ≥10% in bone-marrow cells or peripheral-blood leukocytes qualifies as a B-finding in systemic mastocytosis.
cards.locator: MASTOCYTOSIS — B-finding

cards.interpretation: According to WHO 5th Edition 2022, bone marrow mastocytosis is a systemic mastocytosis subtype characterized by absence of skin lesions and B-findings and basal serum tryptase <125 ng/mL.
cards.locator: MASTOCYTOSIS — bone marrow mastocytosis subtype

cards.interpretation: According to WHO 5th Edition 2022, the term “myelodysplastic neoplasms,” abbreviated MDS, replaces “myelodysplastic syndromes.” MDS is defined as a clonal haematopoietic neoplasm with cytopenia(s) and morphologic dysplasia, with a recommended dysplasia threshold of ≥10% in a lineage.
cards.locator: MYELODYSPLASTIC NEOPLASMS — core definition and dysplasia threshold

cards.interpretation: According to WHO 5th Edition 2022, MDS with low blasts and isolated 5q deletion requires <5% bone-marrow blasts and <2% peripheral-blood blasts, with 5q deletion alone or with one additional abnormality other than monosomy 7 or 7q deletion. An SF3B1 mutation or a TP53 mutation that is not multi-hit does not by itself override the MDS-5q diagnosis.
cards.locator: MYELODYSPLASTIC NEOPLASMS — MDS-5q Table 3

cards.interpretation: According to WHO 5th Edition 2022, MDS with low blasts and SF3B1 mutation is a genetically defined MDS type in which 5q deletion, monosomy 7 and complex karyotype are exclusionary. Detection of ≥15% ring sideroblasts may substitute for an SF3B1 mutation; for SF3B1-wild-type cases with ≥15% ring sideroblasts, “MDS with low blasts and ring sideroblasts” is an acceptable alternative term.
cards.locator: MYELODYSPLASTIC NEOPLASMS — MDS-SF3B1 Table 3

cards.interpretation: According to WHO 5th Edition 2022, MDS with biallelic TP53 inactivation requires <20% blasts in blood and marrow plus either ≥2 TP53 mutations or one TP53 mutation with TP53 copy-number loss or copy-neutral loss of heterozygosity. Two or more TP53 mutations can generally be considered multi-hit status. MDS-biTP53 supersedes MDS-5q and MDS-SF3B1 in the WHO5 genetic hierarchy.
cards.locator: MYELODYSPLASTIC NEOPLASMS — MDS-biTP53 Table 3

cards.interpretation: According to WHO 5th Edition 2022, clinical assessment of biallelic TP53 alteration in MDS uses sequencing covering at least TP53 exons 4–11, generally coupled with assessment of TP53 copy-number status; copy loss may also be inferred by next-generation sequencing.
cards.locator: MYELODYSPLASTIC NEOPLASMS — TP53 biallelic-status testing

cards.interpretation: In MDS, WHO 5th Edition 2022 notes that TP53 VAF ≥50% may be regarded as presumptive, but not definitive, evidence of trans-allelic copy loss or copy-neutral loss of heterozygosity when a constitutional TP53 variant has been excluded.

cards.interpretation: According to WHO 5th Edition 2022, a 20% blast cutoff is retained to delineate MDS from AML, but most AML types with defining genetic abnormalities may be diagnosed below 20% blasts. AML with BCR::ABL1 and AML with CEBPA mutation remain exceptions requiring ≥20% blasts. When a genetically defined AML is diagnosed below 20%, morphologic and molecular findings must be correlated to establish that the defining abnormality is driving the disease.

cards.interpretation: According to WHO 5th Edition 2022, childhood MDS with low blasts replaces the former term refractory cytopenia of childhood and is defined by <5% bone-marrow blasts and <2% peripheral-blood blasts. It comprises hypocellular and NOS subtypes, and diagnosis requires exclusion of non-neoplastic causes of cytopenia, bone-marrow failure syndromes and germline pathogenic variants.

cards.interpretation: According to WHO 5th Edition 2022, childhood MDS with increased blasts is defined by 5–19% bone-marrow blasts or 2–19% peripheral-blood blasts.

cards.interpretation: According to WHO 5th Edition 2022, CMML requires all four prerequisite criteria: persistent absolute peripheral-blood monocytosis ≥0.5 × 10^9/L and relative monocytosis ≥10%; <20% blasts/blast equivalents in blood and marrow; absence of diagnostic criteria for CML or another MPN; and absence of a myeloid/lymphoid neoplasm with a tyrosine-kinase fusion. Supporting criteria are dysplasia in ≥1 myeloid lineage, with ≥10% of cells affected; an acquired clonal cytogenetic or molecular abnormality; and abnormal monocyte partitioning with >94% classical monocytes in the absence of active autoimmune/systemic inflammatory disease. With monocytosis ≥1 × 10^9/L, at least one supporting criterion is required; with monocytosis ≥0.5 but <1 × 10^9/L, both dysplasia and clonality are required. A prior MPN excludes CMML; MPN-type marrow features and/or a high burden of JAK2, CALR or MPL mutations support MPN with monocytosis rather than CMML.
cards.locator: MYELODYSPLASTIC/MYELOPROLIFERATIVE NEOPLASMS — CMML prerequisite monocytosis

cards.interpretation: According to WHO 5th Edition 2022, CMML is subtyped as myelodysplastic CMML when WBC <13 × 10^9/L and myeloproliferative CMML when WBC ≥13 × 10^9/L. Blast-based subgrouping comprises CMML-1 with <5% blasts/promonocytes in blood and <10% in marrow and CMML-2 with 5–19% in blood and 10–19% in marrow; CMML-0 is no longer recognized.
cards.locator: MYELODYSPLASTIC/MYELOPROLIFERATIVE NEOPLASMS — CMML WBC subtypes

For SF3B1-wild-type cases with ≥15% ring sideroblasts, MDS/MPN with ring sideroblasts and thrombocytosis remains acceptable terminology.

cards.interpretation: According to WHO 5th Edition 2022, AML, myelodysplasia-related (AML-MR; formerly AML with myelodysplasia-related changes) requires ≥20% blasts with a myeloid immunophenotype plus at least one qualifying MDS-related feature: a history of MDS or MDS/MPN; a defining somatic mutation in ASXL1, BCOR, EZH2, SF3B1, SRSF2, STAG2, U2AF1 or ZRSR2; or a defining cytogenetic abnormality comprising complex karyotype (≥3 abnormalities), 5q deletion/loss, monosomy 7 or 7q deletion/loss, 11q deletion, 12p deletion/loss, monosomy 13 or 13q deletion, 17p deletion/loss, isochromosome 17q or idic(X)(q13). Morphologic dysplasia alone is insufficient. A diagnosis of acute erythroid leukaemia supersedes AML-MR.

cards.interpretation: According to WHO 5th Edition 2022, AML with minimal differentiation requires blasts negative (<3%) for MPO and SBB by cytochemistry and expression of at least two myeloid-associated antigens such as CD13, CD33 and CD117. It also requires ≥20% blasts, absence of a defining genetic AML type, absence of mixed-phenotype acute leukaemia, absence of myeloid neoplasm post cytotoxic therapy and no prior MPN.

cards.interpretation: According to WHO 5th Edition 2022, AML without maturation requires ≥3% blasts positive for MPO or SBB, NSE negativity, <10% maturing granulocytic cells and expression of at least two myeloid-associated antigens. It also requires ≥20% blasts, absence of a defining genetic AML type, absence of mixed-phenotype acute leukaemia, absence of myeloid neoplasm post cytotoxic therapy and no prior MPN.
cards.locator: ACUTE MYELOID LEUKAEMIA — AML without maturation (Table 9)

cards.interpretation: According to WHO 5th Edition 2022, AML with maturation requires ≥3% blasts positive for MPO or SBB, ≥10% maturing granulocytic cells, <20% monocyte-lineage cells and expression of at least two myeloid-associated antigens. It also requires ≥20% blasts, absence of a defining genetic AML type, absence of mixed-phenotype acute leukaemia, absence of myeloid neoplasm post cytotoxic therapy and no prior MPN.
cards.locator: ACUTE MYELOID LEUKAEMIA — AML with maturation (Table 9)

cards.interpretation: According to WHO 5th Edition 2022, acute basophilic leukaemia requires basophilic blasts/immature or mature basophils with metachromasia on toluidine blue, blasts negative for MPO, SBB and NSE, and absence of strong CD117-equivalent expression. It also requires ≥20% blasts, absence of a defining genetic AML type, absence of mixed-phenotype acute leukaemia, absence of myeloid neoplasm post cytotoxic therapy and no prior MPN.
cards.locator: ACUTE MYELOID LEUKAEMIA — acute basophilic leukaemia (Table 9)

cards.interpretation: According to WHO 5th Edition 2022, acute myelomonocytic leukaemia requires ≥20% monocytes and precursors, ≥20% maturing granulocytic cells and ≥3% blasts positive for MPO. It also requires ≥20% blasts, absence of a defining genetic AML type, absence of mixed-phenotype acute leukaemia, absence of myeloid neoplasm post cytotoxic therapy and no prior MPN.
cards.locator: ACUTE MYELOID LEUKAEMIA — acute myelomonocytic leukaemia (Table 9)

cards.interpretation: According to WHO 5th Edition 2022, acute monocytic leukaemia requires ≥80% monocytes and/or their precursors, <20% maturing granulocytic cells, and blasts/promonocytes expressing at least two monocytic markers among CD11c, CD14, CD36 and CD64 or showing NSE positivity. It also requires ≥20% blasts, absence of a defining genetic AML type, absence of mixed-phenotype acute leukaemia, absence of myeloid neoplasm post cytotoxic therapy and no prior MPN.
cards.locator: ACUTE MYELOID LEUKAEMIA — acute monocytic leukaemia (Table 9)

cards.interpretation: According to WHO 5th Edition 2022, acute erythroid leukaemia is characterized by erythroid predominance, usually ≥80% of marrow cellularity, with ≥30% proerythroblasts; cases with <80% erythroid cellularity are recognized when they share the same clinicopathologic features. “Pure erythroid leukaemia” is retained as an acceptable related term. The other shared differentiation-defined AML exclusions apply, but the ≥20% blast requirement does not.
cards.locator: ACUTE MYELOID LEUKAEMIA — acute erythroid leukaemia

cards.interpretation: According to WHO 5th Edition 2022, acute megakaryoblastic leukaemia requires blasts expressing at least one platelet glycoprotein marker—CD41, CD61 or CD42b. It also requires ≥20% blasts, absence of a defining genetic AML type, absence of mixed-phenotype acute leukaemia, absence of myeloid neoplasm post cytotoxic therapy and no prior MPN.
cards.locator: ACUTE MYELOID LEUKAEMIA — acute megakaryoblastic leukaemia (Table 9)

cards.interpretation: According to WHO 5th Edition 2022, AML with other defined genetic alterations provides a classification category for uncommon or emerging genetically defined AML subtypes, including rare genetic fusions; CBFA2T3::GLIS2 is recognized in this category in the acute megakaryoblastic leukaemia context.
cards.locator: ACUTE MYELOID LEUKAEMIA — AMKL/RAM immunophenotype

cards.interpretation: According to WHO 5th Edition 2022, a myeloid neoplasm post cytotoxic therapy (MN-pCT) is diagnosed when criteria for AML, MDS or MDS/MPN are fulfilled in a patient with a documented history of chemotherapy or large-field radiation therapy for an unrelated neoplasm. CCUS is excluded. NPM1-mutated disease and core-binding-factor leukaemias with RUNX1::RUNX1T1 or CBFB::MYH11 still receive the post-cytotoxic designation when the exposure history is present. PARP1 inhibitors qualify as an exposure and methotrexate does not. The specific myeloid diagnosis should be given when possible with “post cytotoxic therapy” appended.

cards.interpretation: In AML or MDS post cytotoxic therapy, biallelic/multi-hit TP53 alterations—including ≥2 TP53 mutations or a TP53 mutation with 17p/TP53 deletion or copy-neutral loss of heterozygosity—are associated with worse outcomes.

The framework includes: without a pre-existing platelet disorder or organ dysfunction—germline CEBPA, DDX41 or TP53 pathogenic/likely pathogenic variants; with a pre-existing platelet disorder—germline RUNX1, ANKRD26 or ETV6 pathogenic/likely pathogenic variants; and with potential organ dysfunction—including germline GATA2, SAMD9 or SAMD9L pathogenic/likely pathogenic variants and biallelic germline BLM pathogenic/likely pathogenic variants. cards.interpretation: According to WHO 5th Edition 2022, myeloid/lymphoid neoplasms with eosinophilia and tyrosine kinase gene fusions (MLN-TK) are BCR::ABL1-negative neoplasms driven by defining tyrosine-kinase rearrangements; eosinophilia is common but is not required. Defining abnormalities include rearrangements of PDGFRA, PDGFRB, FGFR1, JAK2 or FLT3; ETV6::ABL1; and other defined fusions including ETV6::FGFR2, ETV6::LYN, ETV6::NTRK3, RANBP2::ALK, BCR::RET and FGFR1OP::RET. MLN-TK supersedes other myeloid or lymphoid diagnoses and systemic mastocytosis in the diagnostic hierarchy, must be excluded before diagnosing CEL, and MLN-TK with ETV6::ABL1 should be distinguished from B-ALL with ETV6::ABL1.

cards.interpretation: According to the IPSS-M framework for MDS, multihit TP53, KMT2A (MLL) partial tandem duplication, FLT3 ITD/TKD, SF3B1 mutation with isolated del(5q), and mutations in NPM1, RUNX1, NRAS, ETV6, IDH2, CBL, EZH2, U2AF1, SRSF2, DNMT3A, ASXL1, and KRAS are main-effect molecular findings that individually contribute adverse prognostic weight. SF3B1a—SF3B1 mutation without BCOR, BCORL1, RUNX1, NRAS, STAG2, SRSF2, or del(5q)—is a main-effect finding that individually contributes favourable prognostic weight. A main-effect finding is modelled individually in IPSS-M, so its gene-specific prognostic contribution is incorporated directly rather than through the residual mutation count.
